page.title: Virtual Event Production: What to Decide First
page.description: Learn the first decisions for virtual event production: platform choice, broadcast setup, accessibility, backup paths, and avoiding single points of failure.
page.h1: What should you decide first about virtual event production?
page.definition: Virtual event production is the end-to-end process of designing, rehearsing and delivering a live online experience using a streaming platform, a run of show, branded assets, a live producer and a backup stream.
page.quick_answer: Choose your platform and production model together, then lock the run of show owner and backup stream before you finalize the agenda.

sections.h2: Which platform and cost model fit your event type?

blocks.p: Match the platform to your event scale and budget by choosing among three cost models. Per-host licences sized by attendee capacity suit Zoom Webinars. Self-serve monthly plans cover StreamYard and Livestorm. Annual contracts quoted by sales apply to ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo and Goldcast. The platform is not the production; someone still has to own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready.

ul: Per-host licences sized by attendee capacity (Zoom Webinars)
Annual contracts quoted by sales (ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast)

sections.h2: What production roles and deliverables do you need?

blocks.p: Define the crew size and deliverable list before you book speakers or build the agenda. One producer can run a simple webinar. Summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator. Standard deliverables cover the full live lifecycle from brief to replay.

ul: Run of show and speaker brief with rehearsal
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Backup stream on a second encoder
Edited recording and short clips for replay

sections.h2: How do you structure the timeline and workstreams?

blocks.p: Map eight workstreams with single owners to keep a summit or webinar on track. A summit needs six to eight weeks of management; a webinar three to four. Lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final. Typical tools include Zoom Events, Cvent or Bizzabo for the event; Eventbrite or Cvent for registration; Asana or Monday.com for the plan; HubSpot or Salesforce for follow-up.

sections.h2: What rehearsal and backup steps prevent failure?

blocks.p: Run one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before live and keep a backup stream ready. A technical check 60 minutes before going live catches last-minute issues. Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours while attendees still remember the event. A single point of failure in the primary stream can end the event; the backup activates within seconds if the main feed drops.

ol: Full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before
Backup stream configured on second encoder or platform
Single point of failure review for every critical path

sections.h2: When should you bring in a production partner?

blocks.p: Hire a production crew when your event needs a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator simultaneously. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it. Platform and production are two purchases: the platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. Moderated webinars range from 2,500 to 7,500 per production; executive summits, online conferences and hybrid productions range from 10,000 to 50,000 and above.

faq.q: How much does a moderated webinar production cost?
faq.a: A moderated webinar production ranges from 2,500 to 7,500 per event based on West Peek Productions published range. This covers run of show, speaker rehearsal, branded assets, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream and edited recording. Platform fees are separate.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for a virtual summit?
faq.a: A virtual summit needs six to eight weeks from kickoff to live date. This includes platform lock, speaker briefing, run of show creation, rehearsal and technical checks. A repeat webinar format can move faster in three to four weeks.

faq.q: Do I need a backup stream for a simple webinar?
faq.a: Yes. Every live event should have a backup stream configured on a second encoder or platform. A single point of failure in the primary stream can end the event. The backup activates within seconds if the main feed drops.

faq.q: What deliverables should I expect from a production partner?
faq.a: Expect a run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and short clips for replay. These are standard whether the event runs on Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard.

faq.q: How do platform and production purchases differ?
faq.a: The platform is software you license per host, per month or per annual contract. Production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. West Peek Productions does not sell software; it produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it.
